contract: Road user u is one of a file of road users travelling one behind another at the observation: counting u itself, at least the minimum member count of road users have their heading aligned with u's within the same-direction tolerance, lie ahead of or behind u in the same lane, and are within the file reach of u, a distance the caller sets measured between the nearest points of the bodies. It is a relation of place, direction and spacing at the observation. It says nothing of why the road users travel together, of a common destination or origin, of an organizer, or of their speed: a caller that means a moving file states the motion itself. Not a stand-in for: a chain each of whose consecutive spaces is bounded — the reach is measured from u to each member, so a long file is read through the membership of each road user in turn — the class of the members, which the caller states, or a towed combination, which is one road user drawn by another.

params.name: min_member_count
params.meaning: the number of road users, u included, at which the group is read as a file rather than as road users happening to follow one another

params.name: file_reach
params.meaning: the distance between the nearest points of two bodies within which another road user is read as travelling with u in the same file

params.name: same_direction_tolerance
params.meaning: the cosine of the largest angle between two headings still read as the same direction, a ratio between minus one and one

elements.span: have their heading aligned with u's within the same-direction tolerance
elements.justification: rel.same_direction is “headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance”, the relation this clause states, the tolerance being the atom's own parameter.

elements.span: lie ahead of or behind u in the same lane
elements.justification: rel.ahead_behind_in_lane is “a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction”, which is the one-behind-another arrangement this clause states; rel.bearing is not read, giving only a direction and not an in-lane order.

elements.span: are within the file reach of u, a distance the caller sets measured between the nearest points of the bodies
elements.justification: rel.surface_gap is the “distance between the nearest points of two bodies, each body's footprint read with its own heading and extent”, which is the spacing this clause bounds; rel.centre_distance is excluded by its own contract as “not a stand-in for a clearance between bodies”.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: Five cars run in file in one lane of a rural highway, each within 20 m of the next and all headings aligned: each of them, counting itself, has at least three members of the group within the reach, ahead of or behind it in the lane.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: One car runs alone in that lane with the nearest other road user 400 m ahead: the minimum member count is not reached within the reach.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The five cars with the source declaring the gap between bodies absent: how far apart the members are, and so how many lie within the reach, cannot be read.
